# dsh-plugin-mcp-session-meta
Makes **DeepSeek Harness** tell MCP servers *which conversation* is calling.

Every `tools/call` the harness sends gets the calling Agent's session id in
`params._meta.session_id

`. That is the one piece of information an MCP server
needs to keep per-conversation state — and the
one DSH currently leaves blank.

> Chinese documentation: README.zh.md.
> This is an **unofficial community plugin** — not affiliated

with or endorsed by
> DeepSeek.
## The problem

DSH's MCP client passes `{ name, arguments }` straight through as the request
params, leaving `_meta

params, leaving `_meta` empty:

But `_meta` is a first-class optional field of MCP's `BaseRequestParamsSchema`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

So a server can only ever see *the process*, never *the conversation*. For a
server whose state is p

er-conversation — browser automation with tab groups,
editors, anything with sessions — every conver

sation in the harness shares one
bucket and the server has no way to tell them apart.

Other MCP clients already send it: ZCode sends `session_id`, Antigravity sends
`antigravity.google/c

onversation_id`, Codex sends `thread_id`, WorkBuddy sends
`workbuddy.ai/conversationId`. DSH is the

id`, Codex sends `thread_id`, WorkBuddy sends
`workbuddy.ai/conversationId`. DSH is the odd one out.

The identity is already sitting at the call site — the agent loop sets
`ToolExecutionInput.agent` (*

"The agent on whose behalf the call runs"*), and
`agent.id` **is** the SessionId. It is simply not f

t on whose behalf the call runs"*), and
`agent.id` **is** the SessionId. It is simply not forwarded.
## What it changes
Two patches, both in the derived artifact:
| Patch | Before | After |
| `clientInfo` | `{ name: "dsh-mcp-client", version: "0.0.1" }` — a middleware self-report with a pl

aceholder version | `{ name, title: "DeepSeek Harness", version: "<real>" }` |
| `tools/call` params
| `{ name, arguments }` | `{ name, arguments, _meta: { session_id: <agent.id> } }` |

`_meta` is omitted entirely when there is no Agent on the execution (nested
dispatches) — a missing

key means "this frame doesn't know", which is different
from claiming a session.
## Install

The artifact has to be regenerated against **your** installed DSH, because the
patch targets DeepSee
k's *compiled* bundle and that changes between releases.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Then **restart DSH** — see *Caching* below.

- `--profile web` — target another profile (default `desktop`)
- `--check` — report only, change not

hing
- `--uninstall` — put the entry back to the upstream package

Only the entry you name is switched; other MCP servers keep using the upstream
client. Nothing else
in the harness changes.
### Caching: a restart is required

DSH caches imported plugin modules. Editing plugin code — or even changing which
package an entry po

ints at — does **not** take effect live: Node's ESM cache is
keyed by URL, and the plugin manager's

enable/disable only re-runs `apply()` on
the already-imported module. A restart (or a brand-new entr

y id) is the only
thing that re-imports. Expect "the entry is active, the module name changed, and
i
t still runs the old code" until you restart.
## Compatibility

- Built and tested against `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` **0.2.0-rc.2**
(DeepSeek Harness 0.2.0-rc.2

, macOS).
- `sync.mjs` asserts on both patch anchors. If a DSH upgrade moves them it
**fails** rathe

r than emitting an unpatched artifact — a silently unpatched
copy is the worst outcome here, because

the plugin would still load and simply
stop doing anything.
- Node ≥ 22.15 (extraction uses `zlib.z
stdDecompressSync`).
## How it is built (and why not a plain fork)

DeepSeek's harness repository does not accept external pull requests, and the app
bundle is code-sig

ned with per-file integrity hashes — editing files inside
`app.asar` breaks the signature and is ove
rwritten by every update.

So the artifact is **extracted, patched and regenerable** rather than a frozen
copy:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`sync.mjs` also reads the external modules the bundle imports and writes them
into `peerDependencies

`. That is not bookkeeping: DSH's profile resolver supplies
packages **by peer declaration** ("Linke

d importers apply current peer
declarations at each ancestor node_modules"). An undeclared peer is n

ot supplied,
and the plugin dies during import with no useful error. Deriving the list from
the arti
fact keeps it in step automatically.
## Notes for other DSH plugin authors
Two things that cost real time to discover:

1. **Declare every package you import as a `peerDependency`.** The resolver in
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-app

-boot` reads the importing package's own manifest to
decide what to supply. Miss one and the fiber e

nds up `DISPOSED` with a bare
`fiber state 4` and no message.
2. **`patchReload: "live"` is a profil

e setting.** The shipped `web` profile has
it; a profile without it will not pick up patch edits wit

e shipped `web` profile has
it; a profile without it will not pick up patch edits without a restart.
## When to delete this

When DSH forwards the session id itself. The upstream fix is small — the identity
is already in scop

e at the call site — and this plugin exists only to fill the gap
in the meantime.

That request is filed here, with the exact change and the evidence:
**https://github.com/deepseek-ai
/deepseek-harness/discussions/9519**
If it lands, this package is dead weight — uninstall it.
